title: intervention
description: Someone had to step in where the plan did not foresee it: a person (an owner op, a push, a hand merge, a rescue), the loop's judge (the main conversation, running a control op through the control tool) or the loop with unplanned judgement or recovery (a triage, an unknown step, a park, a guard refusal). Written by the loop, and by hand for a rescue the loop cannot see. Not a stage and not progress. The issue is null for a fleet-level one (a restart, a settings edit). Count one per (issue, cause, fact); each row with a null fact counts. A ci-rerun row carrying flaky records the re-run's result as a second row for the same fact, so it still counts once as an intervention under that key.

who.description: person: a person did something; loop: the loop had to judge or recover; judge: the loop's judge (the main conversation) ran a control op through the control tool.

cause.description: What happened, as a code of v2 SPEC 7.2: for example op:resume, push, hand-merge, rescue, restart, config-file, triage, park, unknown:timeout, free:load, fix:ci or guard:write. An open list: handle a code you do not know.

life.description: The issue's life it happened in, as in transition; null when none applies.

fact.description: The key of the fact it records, so it is logged and counted once; null for a hand-recorded rescue.

pr.description: The pull request involved, when there is one.

flaky.description: On a ci-rerun row recording the re-run's result: true when the re-run passed on the same head as the failure; false when it failed again. Null otherwise.

failed_tests.description: The names of the tests that failed in the CI run. Null when none were recorded.

failed_jobs.description: The names of the CI jobs that failed. Null when none were recorded.

head.description: The commit the CI run was on, when known.

detail.description: One line for people saying what happened; empty when none was given. Never parse it.

examples.detail: a fixer for a merge conflict on PR #83, from reviewing
